Principle: Variable Detection
Conducts a theoretically relatively safe experiment at a theoretically relatively safe yield, dealing AoE Electro DMG and creating a Detection Core in different ways depending on whether the Skill is tapped or held.

Constellations

The Observer Seeking What Is Missing
The maximum number of Gradient Beacons Mitya can carry is increased to 5. Using the Elemental Skill Principle: Variable Detection additionally creates 1 Gradient Beacon.
While the Detection Core is present, the nearbyyour own active character's CRIT DMG is increased by 50%40%.
Additionally, Mitya regenerates 10 Elemental Energy when a Gradient Beacon is created. This effect can be triggered once every 8s.
The Matter That Slumbers Beyond Inertness
While the Detection Core is present, all opponents within the Polestar Field have their Cryo RES and Electro RES decreased by 20%.
Additionally, if the Detection Core created is:
·Steady State: All nearby party members gain 100123 Elemental Mastery;
·Overloaded: Your active character gains 200234 Elemental Mastery.
The Isotopes Born of Decay
Detection Cores created by Mitya himself deals 1 instance of AoE Electro DMG equal to 400%300% of Mitya's Elemental Mastery to nearby opponents for every 5 Gradient Beacons consumed while it is on the field. This DMG is considered Stellar-Conduct reaction DMG.
Elemental Transition at the Gate of Reason
Detection Core is enhanced. If the Detection Core:
· Is in the Steady State: Detection Core deals 115% of its original DMG.
· Is Overloaded: There is a 30%34% chance to create 1 new Gradient Beacon whenever Mitya consumes a Gradient Beacon with the Detection Core.
Additionally, Stellar-Conduct reaction DMG dealt by all nearby party members is Elevated by 20%.

Rule Terms

Gradient Beacons
When Mitya is in the party, Stellar-Conduct reactions create Gradient Beacons that last for 6s instead of Starlight Prisms. Mitya can consume Gradient Beacons to trigger various effects.
Gradient Beacons follow the active character and transform the nearby area into a Polestar Field when the Gradient Beacon is created. Mitya can have multiple Gradient Beacons, with an initial maximum of 4. Creating a Gradient Beacon while at the maximum will reset the duration of all Gradient Beacons.
Before 7.1.52

Veil of Falsehood

Subzero Conditioning
Valeriy enters the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state while within a Polestar Field.

Rule Terms

Polestar Field
When Stellar-Conduct is triggered, the surrounding area will transform into a Polestar Field for a short period of time, and when inside a Polestar Field, certain characters will enter the Radiance: Stellar-Conduct state, which grants various skill buffs.
Direct-Fire Mortar: Point-Blank Bombardment
Valeriy's special Charged Attack. Using a Charged Attack while he has at least 40 Impact Momentum consumes all Impact Momentum to unleash this special Charged Attack instead, dealing AoE Electro DMG in front of him and granting 15 stacks of Offensive Directive.
Within 0.8s after using the Elemental Skill Active Defense: Bastion Charge or the Elemental Burst Focused Fire: Lightning Salvo, if Valeriy has at least 40 Impact Momentum, the next Normal Attack he uses will be converted to the special Charged Attack Direct-Fire Mortar: Point-Blank Bombardment.
Before 7.1.52

Related Content

Description "Emergency Barricade" Valeriy's specialty. A loaf of rye bread so hard it could double as a makeshift barricaderifle rest in a trench, support a rifle, or simply be hurled at an enemy to knock them senseless. Drop it into hot soup, however, and the rich aroma of rye slowly begins to bloom. Once it has soaked up the broth, the rock-hard loaf turns soft, tender, and surprisingly delicious... It is almost miraculous. Even a seasoned army cook might have to admit defeat.
Effect "Emergency Barricade" Restores 26% of Max HP to the selected character and regenerates 570 HP every 5s for 30s.

Rule Terms

Sword Essence
The energy required to use the special Elemental Skill Windborne Sword while in the Armed for Action mode.
Vesna can accumulate Sword Essence in the following ways:
· By performing a Normal Attack, Charged Attack, or Plunging attack while in the Armed for Action mode, or by unleashing Windborne Sword: Transpose from the Constellation Unwavering Ardor;
· By using the Elemental Skill The Art of Victory; or
· By using the Elemental Burst For the Tsaritsa!

Stories

Character Story 5
Unlocks at Friendship Lv. 6
Those three days were anything but peaceful for Vesna.
The proud history of her family, once a source of such certainty, had begun to crumble before her eyes. And before she could fully come to terms with that bitter truth, one question after another came crowding into her mind.
Why did the Tsaritsa choose to name her? Why did that fragment of sacred authority awaken within her?
Why did the Mayor himself come all this way simply to answer her doubts? And what did the Tsaritsa truly intend by sending him?
What question would she be answering three days from now? And would the answer she gave be one they could accept?
More troubling was the history her family had spent so many years carefully dressing up. The Tsaritsa had never once seen fit to expose the truth, and yet now, she hadnow revealed it all to Vesna with such ease that it startled her...
Could she be planning something against her grandfather, perhaps even against House Strivozha? And if so, would Vesna be forced to choose between her family and the Tsaritsa?
Vesna dared not follow that thought any further. Nor could she bring herself to voice these suspicions to her parents or her grandfather. But if matters truly came to what she feared, then somewhere in the silence of her heart, she had already made her choice.
Three days passed, and the two met again in the study as promised. Vesna sat rigidly at the desk, unable to keep the look of someone ready for battle from her face.
The Mayor shook his head, "Good evening, my dear Miss Fern. You don't mind if I still call you that, do you?"
Vesna blinked. After learning the uglier chapters of her family's history, she had expected herself to recoil instinctively from the name.
But she didn't. If anything, the moment she heard it, the first thing that came to mind was her mother's gentle and caring face.
"...My little flame fern... My love for you will last forever..."
Tears suddenly glimmered at the corners of Vesna's eyes. "Me too, Mother," she whispered. Then, as though some momentous decision had just been made, she raised her head and spoke each word with unwavering resolve.
"Sir, I will not betray my mother. I will not betray House Strivozha. And I will never betray Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, who gave me my name."
"If Her Majesty can no longer believe in the loyalty and honor of House Strivozha, then let my blood restore them."
"Don't ask me what my answer is. It's right here!"
With that, Vesna drew a dagger and drove it into the table between them. Then she stiffened her neck, squeezed her eyes shut, and solemnly presented herself like some valiant martyr awaiting the blade.
Pulcinella stared at the scene before him, momentarily dumbfounded. He quickly cleared his throat several times. "Miss Vesna... I believe there may have been a misunderstanding."
"The question Her Majesty wanted me to ask you was: What is love?"
Vesna's eyes flew wide, still bright with unshed tears. "What? What do you mean? What's the question?"
"Well... Her Majesty is, after all, the god who presides over love. She simply wished to know what love means in your eyes, Miss Vesna."
"Think of it as the sort of thing a mother might casually ask her child while they were out on a pleasant trip together. You know, Her Majesty chose your name herself, and she has always been rather fond of you."
"Oh... I don't mean to suggest that Her Majesty wishes to be your mother, of course. Though she has been keeping an eye on your growth all these years... But you already have a wonderful mother of your own."
"Er... In any case... I'm sure you can treat it as a perfectly ordinary question. Please don't read too much into it."
The Mayor chose his words with great care, wary of giving the imaginative young Vila any more ideas she might run away with.
Yet faced with his question, Vesna found there was nothing to think about. She had never been asked it before, but the answer had been part of her life for as long as she could remember.
"Vesna, my brave little snowball flower..." "Vesna, my lucky little lilac..." "Vesna, my clever little cornflower..."
...
Once more, she heard the sweet little stories her mother had woven for her. Not even a second passed before she gave the answer.
"Love is creation! It's the power to create strength for those we cherish, to create laughter, courage, and hope. Yes, love is creation."
...
The Mayor left the Strivozha estate with a joyful expression on his face.
He couldn't say whether Her Majesty would be pleased with Vesna's answer, but he himself had a good feeling about it — and about Vesna too, that charming little girl who seemed to carry spring wherever she went.
Before departing, he had made a point of telling Grand Duke Pyotr that he was no longer to oversee Vesna's education. Her Majesty, it seemed, already had something far more suitable in mind.
Perhaps in a week's time, Vesna would become his student in earnest. Perhaps a year from now, she would take her seat as the youngest councilor ever to serve on the Snezhnograd Veche.
Whatever the future held, Pulcinella was certain that after tonight, warmth and laughter would return at last to the once silent and joyless Vila estate. After all, "Vesna" was never meant to describe winter.
"Vesna, Vesna... There is an unconquerable spring within you. May you one day help Her Majesty create a world with much love in it."
Before 7.1.52

More troubling was the history her family had spent so many years carefully dressing up. The Tsaritsa had never once seen fit to expose the truth, and yet now, she hadnow revealed it all to Vesna with such ease that it startled her...
Could she be planning something against her grandfather, perhaps even against House Strivozha? And if so, would Vesna be forced to choose between her family and the Tsaritsa?
Vesna dared not follow that thought any further. Nor could she bring herself to voice these suspicions to her parents or her grandfather. But if matters truly came to what she feared, then somewhere in the silence of her heart, she had already made her choice.
Three days passed, and the two met again in the study as promised. Vesna sat rigidly at the desk, unable to keep the look of someone ready for battle from her face.
The Mayor shook his head, "Good evening, my dear Miss Fern. You don't mind if I still call you that, do you?"
Vesna blinked. After learning the uglier chapters of her family's history, she had expected herself to recoil instinctively from the name.
But she didn't. If anything, the moment she heard it, the first thing that came to mind was her mother's gentle and caring face.
"...My little flame fern... My love for you will last forever..."
Tears suddenly glimmered at the corners of Vesna's eyes. "Me too, Mother," she whispered. Then, as though some momentous decision had just been made, she raised her head and spoke each word with unwavering resolve.
"Sir, I will not betray my mother. I will not betray House Strivozha. And I will never betray Her Majesty the Tsaritsa, who gave me my name."
"If Her Majesty can no longer believe in the loyalty and honor of House Strivozha, then let my blood restore them."
"Don't ask me what my answer is. It's right here!"
With that, Vesna drew a dagger and drove it into the table between them. Then she stiffened her neck, squeezed her eyes shut, and solemnly presented herself like some valiant martyr awaiting the blade.
Pulcinella stared at the scene before him, momentarily dumbfounded. He quickly cleared his throat several times. "Miss Vesna... I believe there may have been a misunderstanding."
"The question Her Majesty wanted me to ask you was: What is love?"
Vesna's eyes flew wide, still bright with unshed tears. "What? What do you mean? What's the question?"
"Well... Her Majesty is, after all, the god who presides over love. She simply wished to know what love means in your eyes, Miss Vesna."
"Think of it as the sort of thing a mother might casually ask her child while they were out on a pleasant trip together. You know, Her Majesty chose your name herself, and she has always been rather fond of you."
"Oh... I don't mean to suggest that Her Majesty wishes to be your mother, of course. Though she has been keeping an eye on your growth all these years... But you already have a wonderful mother of your own."
"Er... In any case... I'm sure you can treat it as a perfectly ordinary question. Please don't read too much into it."
The Mayor chose his words with great care, wary of giving the imaginative young Vila any more ideas she might run away with.
Yet faced with his question, Vesna found there was nothing to think about. She had never been asked it before, but the answer had been part of her life for as long as she could remember.
"Vesna, my brave little snowball flower..." "Vesna, my lucky little lilac..." "Vesna, my clever little cornflower..."
...
Once more, she heard the sweet little stories her mother had woven for her. Not even a second passed before she gave the answer.
"Love is creation! It's the power to create strength for those we cherish, to create laughter, courage, and hope. Yes, love is creation."
...
The Mayor left the Strivozha estate with a joyful expression on his face.
He couldn't say whether Her Majesty would be pleased with Vesna's answer, but he himself had a good feeling about it — and about Vesna too, that charming little girl who seemed to carry spring wherever she went.
Before departing, he had made a point of telling Grand Duke Pyotr that he was no longer to oversee Vesna's education. Her Majesty, it seemed, already had something far more suitable in mind.
Perhaps in a week's time, Vesna would become his student in earnest. Perhaps a year from now, she would take her seat as the youngest councilor ever to serve on the Snezhnograd Veche.
Whatever the future held, Pulcinella was certain that after tonight, warmth and laughter would return at last to the once silent and joyless Vila estate. After all, "Vesna" was never meant to describe winter.
"Vesna, Vesna... There is an unconquerable spring within you. May you one day help Her Majesty create a world with much love in it."

Vodyanitsa

★★★★★
Open detail page

Stories

Character Story 1
Unlocks at Friendship Lv. 2
Once, Vodyanitsa sang with a joy as bright and untroubled as the childhood her kin had shared in Dalegrad.
In those days, the Water Imps knew no bounds. They wandered wherever their hearts desired, giving freely their songs of blessing to every living thing.
...Then Vodyanoy DombertievDonbettyr, the Lackland, entered into league with King Miscislav the Blood-Devourer. The swift and fearless children of the waters became the strength behind Miscislav's ascent, winning him glory and, in time, a crown. Yet Dombertiev'sDonbettyr's daughter, Vaselisa Vodyanovna, could not bear the sight of her kin's cold blood frozen across the lake. With blood-pink flowers of ice cupped in her hands, she stood upon the water's edge and mourned each silent soul.
At last, she departed. All among her kin who would no longer bear arms followed in her wake, and together they made their way to the court of Emperor Monomakh Snezhnyi.
There, the Emperor conferred a title upon her. Vaselisa Vodyanovna accepted it, for she knew that if she wished to receive the favor of the Pale Star, she must first bear the name bestowed upon her.
Yet when crown, treasure, and lands were offered to her in turn, Vodyanovna refused them all. The exiled Water Imp said only to the Tsar:
"I have no need of this crown, for it can rest only upon a brow weighed down by a heart just as still."
"I have no need of this treasure, for it can satisfy only those who chase after empty gain."
"I have no need of these lands, for waters and earth were never meant to belong to any one sovereign."
"I ask for nothing else. I wish only that the children of the waters cease whetting their blades to songs of sorrow. Let them sing for every soul that carries true love within, and let every song they raise belong to their own hearts alone."
Emperor Monomakh assented to Vaselisa Vodyanovna's petition, and from that day onward, no Water Imp beneath the Pale Star would ever again be made to serve the desire of another heart. The Emperor and Vodyanovna bound themselves by oath as well: Even should a Water Imp freely offer to go to war, none would be required to bear steel. And so the covenant was kept. Weaponless, the Water Imps walked among armies without ever joining in the slaughter. Yet neither did they forget the protection Monomakh had granted them.
They became couriers of tidings, bearing military dispatches from camp to camp and the whispered letters of lovers from heart to distant heart — the latter being, by all accounts, their favorite charge. They carried the wounded swiftly downriver, guiding and drawing their rafts with such mastery that it seemed little short of miraculous. And when terror prowled the camps beneath the cover of night, their songs lulled anxious soldiers into peaceful sleep. Many of those tunes outlived the war and passed into the musical canon.
In time, there came a day when no blood darkened the waters of the lake, and the Pale Star cast its radiance unto the furthest reaches of the land. The long lament beneath the snows reached its final verse, and upon the frozen banks of Dalegrad, the blood-pink flowers of ice never rose again.
Then Vaselisa Vodyanovna gathered the Water Imps before her and spoke to them plainly:
"Go. Sing as freely as the waters run, for every precious thing beneath the sky, and for every sincere heart that holds this world dear."
"Tell the snows of spring and the blossoms of winter, the autumn sun and the fruits of summer, that never again need anyone lose their way in the passing of the seasons."
"Tell the waters and the earth that all creation may now hear the hymns that should have been sung to it long ago."
"Tell farmer and craftsman, soldier and sovereign, and every soul in between: The world is worthy of love, and worthy of praise."
And so, at last, Snezhnograd rang with the unfettered songs of the Water Imps.
